title: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act section 524B cybersecurity requirements

source.title: FD&C Act section 524B, Ensuring cybersecurity of devices

vulnerability-management-plan.description: Plan and procedures for monitoring, identifying, and addressing postmarket vulnerabilities; owner: PLAT-1656.

vulnerability-assessment.description: Assessment of identified vulnerabilities and unresolved software anomalies; owner: PLAT-1619.

sbom.description: SBOM records with component support status and end-of-support dates, from `quoin evidence record --adapter sbom` and `quoin soup report` (PLAT-1517/PLAT-1518).

clauses.title: § 524B(a) Premarket submission cybersecurity information
clauses.text: For a covered submission concerning a cyber device, provide the information FDA requires to show that the device meets the cybersecurity requirements in subsection (b).

clauses.title: § 524B(b)(1) Postmarket vulnerability management
clauses.text: Submit a plan for monitoring, identifying, and addressing postmarket cybersecurity vulnerabilities and exploits within a reasonable time, including coordinated vulnerability disclosure and related procedures.

clauses.title: § 524B(b)(2) Cybersecurity processes and updates
clauses.text: Design, develop, and maintain processes and procedures that provide reasonable assurance that the device and related systems are cybersecure, and make postmarket updates and patches available to address the vulnerabilities described in subparagraphs (A) and (B).

clauses.title: § 524B(b)(2)(A) Regular-cycle updates
clauses.text: Provide device and related-system updates and patches on a reasonably justified regular cycle to address known vulnerabilities that are unacceptable.

clauses.title: § 524B(b)(2)(B) Critical-vulnerability updates
clauses.text: Provide out-of-cycle updates and patches as soon as possible for critical vulnerabilities that could cause uncontrolled risks.

clauses.title: § 524B(b)(3) Software bill of materials
clauses.text: Provide FDA a software bill of materials covering commercial, open-source, and off-the-shelf components in the cyber device.
